 PORTLAND, Ore. - At least 40 people are facing federal charges for conspiring to defraud the United States of more than $3 million in fraudulent food stamp purchases.
 U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford announced multiple new guilty pleas, 11 new indictments and major federal sentences in two large interstate fraud schemes involving stolen Electronic Benefit Transfer account information. The schemes involved stealing EBT card data—often through skimming devices—to make unauthorized purchases of large quantities of food stamp-eligible goods.
 "When SNAP benefits are stolen, real families go without food," Bradford said. "That is unacceptable. My office will continue pursuing these cases to safeguard the integrity of the program and uphold the trust placed in us to protect Oregon's communities."
 In October 2024, a federal grand jury in Oregon charged 17 people in a scheme that stole more than $2.4 million in food stamp benefits. Investigators say that from August 2023 to October 2024, the group used skimmers and other methods to steal EBT card information, then used the stolen accounts to buy large amounts of infant formula, energy drinks and other food stamp-eligible items in Oregon, Washington and California, including through curbside pickup orders. More than 120,000 pounds of goods were purchased with stolen benefits, stored in Oregon and Washington, and then shipped to California to be sold on the black market.
 All 17 people were caught in October 2024. One person, Ana Escalante, who helped transport stolen goods across state lines, was sentenced in September 2026 to 27 months in prison and ordered to pay $2.4 million in restitution. So far, 12 people have been sentenced to a combined 157 months in prison, and two more have pleaded guilty and are awaiting sentencing in December 2026.
 In November 2025, Alexandru Telescu and 11 others were charged in a 26-count federal indictment involving a scheme to steal and use EBT card information. Estimated losses total $700,000. Starting in April 2025, the group used stolen EBT numbers and PINs—and skimmers placed on retail payment terminals—to buy food stamp-eligible items in Oregon, Washington and California. They repeatedly made purchases with victims' benefits, stored some of the items in storage units and shipped others to California in vans and trucks.
 On Sept. 29, Telescu pleaded guilty to access device fraud and aggravated identity theft and is scheduled for sentencing on Jan. 28, 2027. Co-defendants Aramis and Cristina Manolea previously pleaded guilty to conspiracy and were each sentenced in May 2026 to time served plus three years of supervised release.
 On Oct. 7, Bly Gnionsiekan Rodoophe Kehi was indicted by a federal grand jury for conspiracy to commit access device fraud and possession of device-making equipment, alleging he installed skimming devices on Washington County payment terminals to steal customers' card data.
 In September and October 2026, federal grand juries charged 10 additional people with unauthorized use of access devices and aggravated identity theft. Prosecutors allege that each person used stolen EBT card numbers and PINs during 2024. Each case involves more than $1,000 in merchandise obtained using benefits stolen from food stamp recipients. Estimated losses total $143,000.
 A multi-agency partnership—including USDA Office of Inspector General, IRS Criminal Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations, the U.S. Marshals Service, multiple police departments and state agencies—is driving the investigation and prosecution of these cases.
